lead: Tesla / TSLA — buy the Musk dip
smaller: IonQ / IONQ — the quantum chips are here
Solana / SOL — the government reserve coin
Zero-day options / VIX — the crash is coming
why_lead: Tesla is the trade where price and attention coincide on 3 March: the stock closed at $284.65, down 29.65% over 20 sessions, while Morgan Stanley reinstated it as a top pick with a $430 target and Yahoo Finance carried Musk’s 10x profit forecast the same morning. The attention is broad and two-sided (Barron’s, Electrek, CNN, AP, Bloomberg), and the simple story the crowd repeats, that the drawdown is a sale on a profit story that has not changed, is carried by the same headlines.
why_smaller: IonQ is the deepest quantum drawdown in the card (IONQ down 41.48% over 20 sessions), and the Microsoft and Amazon chip coverage of 27 February to 3 March gives retail a simple thesis to repeat.
The reserve named Solana and XRP, the reserve rally reversed on 3 March (SOL down 20.43% in the prior session), and Axios and Fortune carried the retail-facing story.
A record share of zero-day SPX options in February and the crash-bet headlines of 3 March sit against a VIX up 38.65% over 20 sessions, which gives a non-equity trade with its own attention evidence.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR): trending on Yahoo Finance on 3 March and sold hard in late February, but over 20 sessions the card shows it up 1.13%, too small a move for the lead.

Rheinmetall and European defence: the largest surge in the card (up 49.80% over 20 sessions), but the coverage on 3 March is institutional (Bloomberg, Reuters, The Guardian) with no retail-attention headlines behind it, so it is used in the Europe block and the Anticipatory section.
Nuclear and SMR names (OKLO, SMR, NNE): down roughly 30% over 20 sessions with heavy news flow, but little retail attention in the window; used in the utilities and uranium context instead.
TSMC: a Stocktwits headline on 3 March says retail remains bullish, but it is a mega-cap whose catalyst belongs to the semiconductor sector; used as a catalyst name.
Indian small-cap and mid-cap sell-off: heavy attention on 3 March, but the card carries no Indian instruments, so there is no price evidence to anchor a trade.
Hims & Hers: a sharp drawdown with compounding-curb headlines, but a single-name story with less retail attention than Tesla; used as a bearish catalyst.
Gold and silver: safe-haven attention (Mining.com on Americans buying gold), but gold futures are up only 3.15% over 20 sessions, not a surge.
